objective: Implement an immutable one-shot shadow exit candidate from previously established memory and a newly accepted generic later-trigger latch, with exact causal evidence, zero parameters, and synthetic native parity only
summary: A separate diagnostic observer projects accepted generic false-to-true trigger latch transitions into one immutable candidate per lifecycle, captures contemporaneous memory and trigger evidence, and archives on native close. The generic state machine, both predicate formulas, and adapter remain byte-identical. Default is disabled. All 358 synthetic tests and Ruff pass, including complete native parity for four switch configurations and independent task-start parity for three supported policies. No candidate has action authority.
north_star_effect: Exposes the exact causal nomination timestamp for later bounded non-economic behavioral review, without changing an exit, threshold, native output, or granting production authority.

files.change: Created immutable candidate/lifecycle records, pure accepted-transition projection and run-local one-shot diagnostic observer
Attached observer to admission, accepted generic latch/rejection, memory observation and native cleanup; exact predicate diagnostic evidence binding
Added separately disabled candidate switch, guarded construction and separate diagnostic sink; no native trading changes
Created 38 synthetic one-shot, chronology, evidence, isolation, cleanup, determinism and full native-parity cases

implementation.default_configuration: async_exit_candidate_shadow_enabled=False. When false, no candidate object is constructed, no candidate processing occurs, and its diagnostic sink is untouched.
implementation.explicit_dependencies: Candidate mode requires the observable trigger predicate explicitly enabled, which already requires the observable adapter and generic async shadow. The memory predicate may be enabled, or causal explicit memory observations supplied. Trigger-only/no-memory diagnostics remain valid and emit no candidate.
implementation.external_input_boundary: When candidate mode is enabled, external true-trigger observations are rejected before replay: they lack the required snapshot-bound predicate evidence. Explicit causal memory remains supported with optional absent market snapshot identity. External false-trigger inputs retain existing conflict semantics. With candidate mode disabled, existing external-input behavior is unchanged.
event_order: existing completed-bar memory predicate and generic memory API
existing generic trigger API readiness/chronology validation
diagnostic observer of newly accepted latch or typed rejection
native close resets generic sidecar and archives candidate lifecycle
implementation.chronology_authority: observe_async_trigger is unchanged and remains sole authority. The conjunction accepts before/after states from that API and projects the false-to-true transition; it does not implement a second timestamp inequality. Typed not-ready rejections produce suppression diagnostics only and are never queued.
implementation.candidate_time: Exactly the generic first successful trigger latch timestamp, at the replay's actual causal decision boundary. Off-grid completed bars retain their own snapshot close identity but the event is not backdated to that label.
implementation.evidence_binding: At admission/new latch only, exact position_id selects one existing predicate diagnostic record. Exact accepted trigger timestamp selects exactly one recorded true-trigger event. Memory first/latest snapshot identities are captured from exact matching true-memory timestamps if available. No filename, substring, frequency or heuristic binding is used.
implementation.one_shot: Each lifecycle retains the first immutable candidate. Later accepted true triggers increment repeated-trigger diagnostics without replacing evidence or emitting again. A new lifecycle ID starts with no candidate. Closed/reused IDs fail closed.
implementation.delay: memory_to_trigger_delay_hours = (candidate_time - memory_first_seen_time) / one hour; descriptive property only, never a gate, threshold, timeout, score or ranking input.
implementation.regime_context: Not added in V1. Regime does not gate or promote a candidate. The later bounded protocol may define diagnostic context analysis separately without granting action authority.
implementation.suppression_count_semantics: MEMORY_NOT_ESTABLISHED contributes to before-memory suppression; NOT_STRICTLY_LATER contributes to temporal-invalid suppression. These categories are disjoint. Other state-contract errors propagate fail-closed.
implementation.storage: One frozen summary and at most one frozen candidate per lifecycle. Active count includes lifecycles without a candidate; native close marks their summaries archived. No future outcome is stored in candidate records.

validation.within_attempt_repairs: One E501 test-line length issue repaired; initial 36 candidate tests passed, then two additional lifecycle/publication tests were added. No scientific failure, test weakening, separate admission or helper retry occurred.
validation.counts_scope: Each count describes a specific synthetic software fixture, not pooled market observations or a frequency/performance study.
validation.native_parity: PASS: all-disabled, memory-only, memory-plus-trigger, and memory-plus-trigger-plus-candidate outputs have exactly equal complete native trade and daily dataframes, metrics containers and counters for all three supported RD27 policies. This verifies software parity, not economic performance.
